pull_request.title: Add governed bounded stable-cell adapter
pull_request.body:
Canic currently wraps a raw stable cell to enforce declared `Storable` encoding bounds. Add `adapter::BoundedCell` so consumers retain that invariant while consuming committed IC Memory allocations and exclusive leases. It exposes only init/get/set and preserves the upstream cell format and initialization behavior; allocation authority and schema ownership remain upstream/with the application.

Encodings are checked before writes and before decoding retained bytes. Qualification now covers both maximum-size and fixed-size records, including short and long fixed-size replacements. Existing upstream cell bytes are produced through `StableCell`, then reopened as bounded records: valid records are preserved; invalid records refuse opening without rewriting bytes or leaking the allocation lease. Rejected replacements preserve both persisted bytes and the cached record. Unbounded records and oversized initial values remain rejected.

Focused locked/offline validation against Memory 0.47: all four bounded-cell regressions pass on Rust 1.91; strict native library/adapter Clippy, formatting, diff checks, documentation links, dependency boundaries and pins pass. No full release gate, native macOS run, installed Canic migration or instruction measurement was run. Pending notes remain 0.4.1; package versions and dependencies are unchanged.

Canic adoption follows publication together with #2 and #3 and its governed collection migration. No local dependency override is introduced. No PR is merged or release executed here.

issue.title: Provide governed map capacity reservation without cloning allocation leases

repository.name: ic-storage
repository.description: Governed stable collections for Internet Computer applications using IC Memory allocation handles.

issue.body:
Canic's current Memory 0.48 / Storage 0.5 adoption exposes an additional prerequisite beyond #3 (map clear) and #10 (bounded cells).

`canic-core/src/storage/stable/intent.rs` currently retains both an eligibility B-tree and a cloned runtime memory handle. Before admitting a receipt, `reserve_application_eligibility_capacity` pre-grows that map's memory; this prevents growth failure after the receipt path begins. The clone is no longer legal under exclusive allocation leases. Storage's governed map owns the sole handle but exposes neither reservation nor its allocated-page count.

Please provide collection-owned, fallible capacity reservation and an observational allocated-page count without exposing raw backing, mutable handles, or unrestricted constructors. Reservation must preserve existing records and the same live lease on success and failure, and survive reopening. An already sufficient reservation must be effect-free; overflow and denied growth must retain typed errors. Qualification should include a real governed runtime, failed growth, successful insertion after reservation, exclusive-open refusal, drop/reopen and retained records.

Canic also currently computes a pinned 0.7.2 map envelope using minimum five entries per node, 2,378 bytes per allocation and 116 fixed bytes. Layout-dependent reservation arithmetic belongs with Storage. Either supply bounded-entry reservation with a stated guarantee or explicitly specify the caller-owned byte/page contract; do not silently drop the pre-admission capacity check or claim entry capacity from page count alone.

This blocks removal of Canic's cloned map handle. No raw-memory compatibility path is requested. Canic's current selected-feature Core check has 17 storage-family failures after Auth transport and Memory/Timers diagnostic API fixes; this is one concrete cause, not a claim that this API alone completes the migration.

issue.title: Complete governed adapter operations for 0.5.3

repository.name: ic-storage
repository.description: Governed stable collections for Internet Computer applications using IC Memory allocation handles.

issue.body:
Canic's collection migration needs operations that retain IC Memory's exclusive allocation lease. Complete the governed adapter on the current post-B-tree-retirement base: consuming map reservation and page observation, in-place map clearing, consuming vector reset, exact `Memory`/`Bound` exports, and bounded singleton cells.

This consolidates #2, #3 and #10 into one current-base proposal. Map clearing uses `clear`, with no second alias for the older proposed `clear_new` name. Reservation takes an absolute extent in 65,536-byte pages; it does not promise entry capacity. Callers own and qualify their page budgets rather than treating upstream node-layout constants as a supported guarantee. Page observation consumes and returns the map because the substrate exposes its memory only through ownership transfer. No memory extraction or unrestricted constructors are public.

`BoundedCell` preserves upstream cell bytes while checking declared maximum/exact encoding sizes before writes and retained-value decoding. Tests cover unchanged bytes/cached values after rejection, invalid retained records, lease release, and optional records. Allocation authority remains with IC Memory; application schemas and recovery remain with consumers.

Retain the preceding ownership cleanup, including retirement of custom-engine import probes and the standalone allocation-policy assertion. Historical research and the reviewed Shared Tooling snapshot remain intact. Package versions and dependency selection are unchanged; pending notes target compatible 0.5.3. The maintainer's main checkout, index and release refs are preserved.

Validation on Linux with the locked registry graph (Memory 0.48.0 / stable structures 0.7.2): seven adapter tests and six Rustdoc examples pass on Rust 1.91; strict native Clippy, warning-free Rustdoc and Wasm compilation pass. Controlled backing tests prove satisfied reservation performs no growth/writes, typed backing refusal preserves bytes/accounting and the lease, and retry/insertion/cold reopening retain records. Formatting, documentation links, pins, dependency boundaries, licenses, snapshot integrity, release-command substitute checks and diff checks pass. Full release CI, clean-source packaging, native macOS and installed Canic adoption have not been run for this batch. The prior delivered 0.5.2 CI matrix is separate evidence and does not qualify this PR.

Issue #12 remains open: selected upstream returning mutations still extract prior values. No fake discard wrapper or local B-tree fork is added, and no performance gain is claimed.

Closes #11.
